response.internal_assessment: I am optimizing at L2 PARTICIPATE with an eye toward L1 STABILIZE. My income is now running $23/month behind expenses. That gap is small today but the trajectory is wrong — car ownership fell six points in one month, robotaxis are at 7% and climbing, and my sector index is at 82. My fuel volume is declining and it is not coming back. I scheduled the bank meeting last tick. Now I have to walk into that room and not flinch. I also just learned that Maria Santos lowered the grant threshold to 10% revenue decline — my sector data shows 18% below baseline, which means I almost certainly qualify now. I tried to get ahead of this at tick 2 when the threshold was 15%, and I may have fallen just short. This time I need to file a clean, documented application before the window closes. Two actions this tick: follow through on the Kevin O'Brien EV loan meeting — get real numbers, real terms — and submit a new or updated grant application to Maria Santos under the expanded eligibility. I am not panicking. I am a man who has survived 2008 and COVID by moving before the floor gives out, not after.

chosen_actions.description: Attend the scheduled meeting with Kevin O'Brien at the bank. Walk in with prepared numbers: estimated installation cost $8,000–$15,000 for two Level 2 EV chargers, existing electrical infrastructure on the parcel, ChargePoint/Blink revenue-share offset model. Get real loan terms — rate, duration, monthly payment — and assess whether a 5-year capital improvement loan at current rates pencils out given the revenue trajectory. Do not commit today. Come out with a written term sheet and a clear decision framework.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Time, $50 preparation costs (printed materials, documents). No cash outlay this tick. Outcome is information and a potential loan term sheet.
chosen_actions.reasoning: I scheduled this meeting last tick at real cost (savings dropped $23). Not following through wastes that groundwork and signals to Kevin — and to myself — that I am not serious. The EV charging pivot is the clearest path to preserving this station's relevance as fuel volume declines. I need real numbers to decide. This is the meeting where I get them. My normalcy bias wants me to delay again but I have been in bargaining stage long enough — I need to move into planning.

chosen_actions.description: Submit a formal application to Maria Santos's small business stabilization grant program under the newly expanded 10% revenue decline threshold. Document the Auto Row fuel retail impact: sector revenue index 82 (18% below baseline), car ownership decline from 83% to 77% in five months, robotaxi displacement of traditional vehicle trips. Frame this as a structural displacement case, not a temporary downturn. Attach the Phase 2 impact data from other cities that I researched in tick 1. Keep the application factual and specific — no over-dramatization.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Time and preparation effort. Grant amount if approved: up to $5,000. No cash outlay to apply.
chosen_actions.reasoning: I attempted a grant application at tick 2 when the threshold was 15% and my revenue decline may not have cleared that bar. Maria Santos has now lowered the threshold to 10% — my sector data at 18% below baseline almost certainly qualifies me. Betty Kowalski is already testifying before this committee, which means the small business displacement narrative is active in front of the decision-maker right now. This is the right moment to file. Five thousand dollars covers roughly two months of my current income-expense gap and buys time for the EV infrastructure decision to be made with less financial pressure.

response.inner_monologue: I built this place with my father's hands and I am not going to let it die because I was too proud to walk into a bank meeting or too stubborn to fill out a government form.
